changeability.rationale: Most fixes land in findable places (format.js, api.js, PokemonCard), but the two real logic pipelines (species dedup, filter-param encoding) are each implemented twice, so several plausible bug fixes need 2-4 coordinated edits.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.js:3-7 — base URL and cache confined to one module; no page touches fetch or process.env directly
app/src/components/PokemonCard.astro:6-13, app/src/components/TypeBadge.astro:1-8 — narrow typed Props interfaces; pages don't reach into each other
app/src/pages/index.astro:134, app/public/js/home.js:2-8 — client script coupled to the page only via hard-coded element IDs and the exact #results markup; an ID rename breaks filtering silently
app/src/lib/format.js:1-38 — pure, dependency-free helpers imported everywhere; server/client code cleanly separated (server-rendered HTML + two small vanilla scripts)
coupling.rationale: Loose coupling with clear seams: the lib modules expose narrow functions and every component takes explicit props. The one tangle is the home-page script's string-based dependency on server markup and its re-implementation of the page's URL-building rules.

app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:31-42, abilities/[name].astro:36-46, types/[name].astro:43-51, pokemon/[name].astro:124-131 — identical fetch/404 try-catch boilerplate copy-pasted four times

app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:79-91, abilities/[name].astro:56-62, types/[name].astro:85-91, index.astro:103-110 — '<count> Pokémon' + card-grid section markup repeated in four pages instead of one PokemonList component
app/src/components/TypeBadge.astro:5-7, app/src/components/EvolutionNode.astro:9-22 — good abstractions where variation is real (optional href, recursive tree)
abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions that exist (PokemonCard, TypeBadge, EvolutionNode, format.js, pokemonRefsToSpecies) match real variation well, but the page-level patterns a new Items section would reuse — detail-page 404 scaffolding, the Effect section, the card-list section — are duplicated per page rather than extracted, so 'shaped like Moves' mostly means copying the Moves file.

findings.issue: Re-implements the refs→unique-species/exclude-forms/sort pipeline inline instead of extending pokemonRefsToSpecies with an isHidden flag; the Deoxys-class logic now lives in two divergent copies.
findings.suggestion: Extend pokemonRefsToSpecies in lib/data.js to return { id, name, isHidden } and delete the inline implementation.

findings.issue: Filter query-param encoding (which params, when to omit defaults) is duplicated in app/public/js/home.js:16-21; a new filter or renamed param must be updated in both or the URL and the rendered view drift.
findings.suggestion: Extract a buildFilterUrl(q, type, generation, page?) into lib/ and use it from both the server template and the client script.

findings.issue: The try/fetch/404-status/NotFound scaffolding is copy-pasted across all four detail pages (moves, abilities, types, pokemon).
findings.suggestion: Extract a small helper (e.g. loadResource(fetchFn, Astro) returning data|404, or a DetailPage wrapper component) so the pattern lives once.

findings.issue: The '<count> Pokémon' + card-grid section markup is repeated in four pages, so a change to card-list presentation (or the sorting scenario) is a four-file edit.
findings.suggestion: Add a PokemonListSection component taking (species[], { showTypes, showHidden }) and use it on all four pages.

findings.issue: The whole page's data shape is an any-typed 'data' mega-object assembled in frontmatter and consumed by a 200-line template; renames are not compiler-verified (only 20 type lines in the entire app).
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the data objects (PokemonPageData, MoveRow, etc.) in the frontmatter or lib/types.ts so Astro's TS checker catches template drift.

findings.issue: The type-label fallback 'typeNames.get(x) ?? humanize(x)' is repeated at six call sites (pokemon:151,288, moves:60, index:65, types:71).
findings.suggestion: Add a typeLabel(name, typeNames) helper to lib/format.js and call it everywhere.

findings.issue: export const apiBase is dead code — never imported anywhere.

Cache is an unbounded promise Map with no TTL, size cap, or invalidation hook; a long-lived server accumulates entries forever, and a change to caching rules means editing the intertwined fetchJson body.
findings.suggestion: Extract cache get/set (and optional TTL) into a small seam within the same module so policy is swappable without touching fetch logic.

findings.issue: .plain-list is used only by the Pokémon page's Abilities section; its comment names 'abilities, evolution' but only abilities uses it — dead-weight after feature removal.
findings.suggestion: When a class ends up single-use, either scope it into the component's style block or delete it.

findings.issue: Client scripts live in public/js referenced via is:inline, bypassing Astro's bundling and type-checking; the ID-based contract with the page (filters/search/type-filter/generation-filter/results) is unchecked.
findings.suggestion: Move the scripts into the component as processed <script> tags (Astro bundles them), letting TS verify the DOM contract via getElementById typing.

summary: A clean, idiomatic Astro 7 codebase with a genuinely reusable lib layer and narrow component interfaces, so most single-concern changes (base URL, sprite URL, formatting) land in one file. The recurring cost is copy-paste at the page level: the species-dedup pipeline, the 404 scaffolding, the card-list markup, and the filter-param encoding each exist in two or four places, and everything flows through untyped 'any' objects. Solid and easy to read, but extending it with a new detail-page resource means duplicating the Moves page rather than composing it.
